findings.title: Working-hours check is broken: `end` equals `start`, and a single non-matching entry rejects the slot
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()` is identical to `start`. It should use the slot end time, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` test only ever checks the slot start. The surrounding `workingHours.find(...)` returns true, meaning the slot is rejected, if ANY working-hour entry for that weekday does not contain the slot. A user with two blocks on one day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17) therefore has every slot rejected, because it is outside at least one of the blocks. The same happens when multiple per-user entries are passed. The check should reject only if no entry contains the slot. As written it can wrongly remove valid slots, and the working-hours comparison is also done in UTC day/minutes.

findings.title: Date override check rejects slots when there are multiple override ranges on one day
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns true (slot unavailable) as soon as any override on the same date does not contain the slot. Cal.com allows several override ranges on the same day (e.g. 9-11 and 14-16). A slot inside the second range is rejected because it is outside the first. The logic should accept the slot if it fits within any override for that date. It also only compares `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` and `slotEndTime <= start`, so a slot that starts inside the override but ends after the override end is treated as available. The day-matching also compares the slot's UTC date against a start shifted by the negated offset, which is questionable for overrides near midnight.

findings.title: Dead comparison using `===` on dayjs objects
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is always false. The branch is dead code. If the intent was to handle zero-length overrides (a day marked unavailable), it does not work. It should use `.isSame()` or compare timestamps.

findings.title: Parsing `override.start.toString()` is locale-dependent and drops milliseconds
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` formats the Date with the locale-style `Date.toString()` and re-parses it. This is non-ISO and fragile, and it drops milliseconds. `override.timeZone` is optional in the type, so `.tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the default zone for overrides without a timezone. The code should pass `override.start` directly. The offset is also computed twice per override because `.add(offset)` is called separately for hour and minute.

findings.title: Tests do not cover the behaviours the PR claims to fix
findings.body: The new timezone test asserts identical UTC slots for +5:30 and +6:00 organizer/invitee views, so it does not prove that overrides adjust to the attendee timezone. `toHaveTimeSlots` only iterates over actual slots (`every`), so it does not check that the slot count matches. Extra or missing trailing slots can go unnoticed. There is no test for the main fix, date overrides on fixed hosts in round-robin events. There is also no test for multiple blocks or overrides on the same day, which the new availability code mishandles.
